blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Retain the context manager for the process lifetime (assign to a module/process-scoped variable, or use an ExitStack registered via atexit) so the snapshot binding is not GC-unwound immediately after `.__enter__()`.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:556: `compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot(repo_root=repo_root).__enter__()`
bind_operation_snapshot finally at src/rebar/_operation_config.py:247-248: `finally: _active_snapshot.reset(token)` — fires when the discarded generator CM is GC-closed
docstring at __main__.py:546-553 claims the binding stays active 'for the remainder of this process', but nothing retains the CM so the contextvar reset runs immediately
blocking.finding: `_bind_operation_snapshot` calls `compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot(...).__enter__()` on a context-manager object that is never stored. The `_GeneratorContextManager` returned by the `@contextmanager` generator has no other reference, so on CPython it is refcount-collected immediately after `.__enter__()` returns; its finalizer calls `close()`, throwing `GeneratorExit` at the `yield snapshot` inside `bind_operation_snapshot`, which runs `finally: _active_snapshot.reset(token)` and UNBINDS the snapshot before the reconcile pass runs. The pass then executes unbound, defeating the entire purpose of the authoritative binding.
scenarios: Direct `python -m rebar_reconciler` pass where downstream store/config reads expect the bound snapshot's tracker_dir/tickets_branch/tickets_remote to be frozen
blocking.suggested_fix: Store the CM (e.g. `_BOUND_CM = compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot(repo_root=repo_root); _BOUND_CM.__enter__()`) in a module-level global so it outlives the function, or push it onto an `atexit`-closed `contextlib.ExitStack`.
